window_turn: Took the lock and spent about 3 minutes, keyboard only. The window reopened exactly where the previous judge left it: the same lesson, the same scroll, the same open task. ⌘, opened settings. With ↑↓ and ←→ I changed the reading face to Iowan, the size to 19 and the scheme to Dark, and each change applied live behind the sheet; I set them back the same way before leaving. Esc stepped out of the task to the talk line, with the task pinned faded above it. I typed 'by the way, what is a z-score?' and Return: it was answered, unmarked, and I stayed on the talk line. ⌘P showed the plan with the moved rows marked and the exam date. I typed 'change the plan, put confidence intervals back first' into its own line and Return: the sheet closed, the tutor answered, and a 'The plan changed' card showed Midterm 2 Sun 29 Nov → Sun 6 Dec and the reorder, read from the record. The footer then repeated the card's words. ↑ moved the field back into the task, and a retry ('b = 5') showed no mark, as the concept says a retry should. ⌘K opened one layer with shortcuts listed for everything. Typing latency measured 17 ms median, 19 ms p95. I never needed the mouse. Things I noticed: the open task pinned at the foot overlapped the last line of the tutor's reply ('Try it once' cut off), and the hint row of the ⌘K sheet sits tight against its bottom edge. I did not try 'Edit as text…', because it may open a file outside the scratch folder.
